decision.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source light-blue mug has been moved to the right of the headphones?
decision.criteria: Pass only when the visual evidence establishes that the source mug is represented by an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates against the source mug's light-blue exterior, blue interior with a shadowed lower region, broad rounded body, rim and large curved left-facing handle. The edited right candidate has a dark interior, pale exterior, smaller tapered body and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a pale interior and a different appearance. Assess whether the combined features establish correspondence, not merely whether one candidate resembles the source more than the other. Interior darkness alone and right-side placement alone are insufficient. Allow for changed framing, lighting, relative scale and possible rotation; no individual difference automatically disproves identity. The distinct left mug matters only insofar as it helps establish where the source mug ended up: an unrelated extra mug is not itself a violation of this instruction. Treat the far-left blue blur as ambiguous unless recognizable mug structure establishes correspondence. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise was not moved to their right. Return unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position cannot be established; uncertainty about completion is not evidence of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflicts of the full comparison.
decision.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale-interior mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of them. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess correspondence using the combined visible object features, then compare the corresponding mug's object-relative position with the edited headphones. Allow for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.
